full_judgment:
SM Ziaul Karim J: This Rule Nisi was issued, on an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 24-8-2006 (Annexure-E to the writ petition) passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka, in Artha Execution Case No.60 of 2006, conferring title of petitioner's mortgaged property upon the decree holder bank, should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 3. Eventually the suit was decreed ex parte on 18-9-2005. 

 4. The bank, then put the decree in execution in Artha Execution Case No.60 of 2006. The bank tried to sell the mortgaged property in auction by complying with Provisions of law laid down in section 33(1)(2)(3)(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 (briefly as Ain 2003) but no bidder participated in the bid. Then the bank filed an application under section 33(7) of the Ain 2003 before the Adalat for a certificate conferring title of the petitioner's mortgaged property upon the bank. After hearing the learned Judge by the order dated 24-8-2006 allowed the said application and conferred title of the said property upon the bank. 

 7. Mr ARM Shahidul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, seeks to impeach the impugned order on the two-fold arguments. Firstly, the learned Judge of the Adalat without complying the mandatory provisions of law prescribed in section 12(6) of the Ain 2003 decreed the suit ex parte without any lawful authority. Secondly, without due compliance of the Provisions of section 33 of the Ain 2003, the learned Judge of the Adalat issued certificate, conferring title of the petitioner's mortgaged property upon the bank. 

 12. On going to the materials on record it transpires that the bank instituted Artha Rin suit No.67 of 2005 for realisation of Taka 25,06,408 with interest against the defendant. The suit was decreed ex parte on 18-9-2005. The bank then put the decree in execution in Artha Execution Case No.60 of 2006. The bank, then took all measures to sell the mortgaged property in auction with due compliance on the provisions of law prescribed in section 33(1)(2)(3)(4) of the Ain, 2003, but with no effect, inasmuch as no bidder participated in the said auction. We find that section 33(5) of the Ain, 2003 provides that after due compliance of sub-sections (1)(2)(3) and (4) of section 33 of the Ain, 2003 if it is not possible to sell the mortgaged property in auction, then the right and possession of the mortgaged property will be vested upon the bank. Consequently at the instance of the bank the Adalat rightly by exercising power conferred under section 33(7) of the Ain, 2003 passed an order conferring title of the petitioner's mortgaged property upon the bank and directed to issue a certificate to that effect. We are in full agreement with the impugned order or the Artha Rin Adalat.
